question: Should OpenClaw commit to `externalResolution` as a stable public approval-presentation contract for external verifier plugins, including the `allow-once` and `allow-always` decision vocabulary?
rationale: The patch is intentionally behavior-neutral, but its Gateway, Swift, and plugin SDK projections create a long-lived compatibility commitment that ordinary correctness checks cannot decide.

options.title: Adopt the RFC contract
options.body: Accept the narrowly bounded provider-neutral descriptor, rebase it onto current main, and treat its field name and decision literals as supported public API.

options.title: Keep the seam internal for now
options.body: Do not merge the public projections until maintainers are ready to define the external-verifier API and its compatibility policy.

options.title: Narrow the public surface further
options.body: Ask for a revised contract if maintainers want only a generic approval capability rather than verifier-oriented presentation metadata.

recommendation.title: Adopt the RFC contract
recommendation.body: Accept the narrowly bounded provider-neutral descriptor, rebase it onto current main, and treat its field name and decision literals as supported public API.

likelyOwner.reason: The linked tracker identifies Kevin as the person who accepted the RFC defining this ownership boundary.
